tables.hint: Twelve standard clauses for proposals with the days, rounds or share they use and the date each is reviewed; the days to review and a review check fill in by themselves.

demo.title: Proposal validity
demo.wording: This proposal is valid for the number of days shown. After that the fee and the start date may change.

demo.title: Included revision rounds
demo.wording: The fee includes the rounds shown for each design stage. More rounds are billed at the rate card price.

demo.title: Payment schedule
demo.wording: The design fee is invoiced at signing and at each stage. Invoices are due within the days shown.

demo.title: Retainer
demo.wording: A retainer secures the start date. It is credited against the first fee invoice and is not refundable after the concept starts.

demo.title: FF&E deposit
demo.wording: A deposit of the share shown is invoiced when the first purchase order is placed. Balances follow before delivery.

demo.title: Change orders
demo.wording: Work outside the agreed scope is priced in a change order and starts only after the client approves it in writing.

demo.title: Cancellation before concept
demo.wording: If the client cancels before the concept stage, the retainer is kept and no further fee is due.

demo.title: Cancellation after concept
demo.wording: If the client cancels after the concept stage, the fee for the stages completed is due in full.

demo.title: Ownership of drawings
demo.wording: Drawings and specifications are provided for the use of this project only and remain the work of the studio.

demo.title: Client approvals
demo.wording: The client answers each approval request within the days shown. Later answers may move the schedule.

demo.title: Delivery and storage
demo.wording: Items are delivered to the studio store or the site. Storage beyond the days shown may be charged.

demo.title: Photography rights
demo.wording: The studio may photograph the finished project for its own portfolio, with the client permission.

guide: Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: mark-up, fixed fee share, smallest fee, retainer share, target income per hour, reply hours and capacity hours.
Check Team, Clients and Projects. They hold the people, clients and projects that every other sheet looks up.
Fill Rate Card with your services, units, rates and minimum units. Cost and margin per unit fill in from your hour cost.
Fill Room Allowances with the FF&E allowance of each room type at three tiers. Every enquiry shows which tier its budget fits.
Log each enquiry on Enquiries, each first meeting on Consultations and each brief on Design Briefs. Replies, follow-ups and budget fit are checked for you.
Write each proposal on Proposals and its service lines on Proposal Items. Fee share, expiry, chase checks and the signing time fill in.
Compare fee models on Fee Models, then keep Packages and Proposal Terms as your standard offers.
Track Retainers, Follow-up Log, Lost Enquiries, Marketing Results and Referral Partners so you know which source brings paying projects.
Watch Capacity Weeks before you promise a start date, and Pipeline by Month for the yearly picture.
Use the 14 calculators for fees, retainers, budgets, win chance, counter-offers, scope changes, source cost, capacity, revisions and what-ifs.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Sales Dashboard and Charts every week: enquiries, proposals, signings, sources, lost reasons, fee yield and free hours.

listing.title: Interior Designer Enquiries, Proposals and Fee Excel Template: Fee Models, Retainers, Rate Card, Capacity, Win Chance, Pipeline
listing.headline: Turn enquiries into signed projects at a fee that pays
listing.description:
Run the sales side of an interior design studio in one Excel workbook. Enquiries logs every contact with its source, budget and rooms, and tells you which tier the budget fits, whether you replied in time and which follow-up is overdue. Proposals holds each fee proposal with its fee type, fee share of the FF&E (furniture, fittings and equipment) budget, expiry and who to chase, and Proposal Items prices every service line from your Rate Card.

Fee Models and the Design Fee Calculator put a fixed fee, an hourly estimate and a percentage fee side by side and show the studio income per hour of each, so you know before you sign whether a fee reaches your target. Room Allowances turn a client budget into a tier, and Budget Reality Check shows the gap and how the budget splits across categories.

Consultations, Design Briefs, Follow-up Log, Lost Enquiries, Retainers, Packages, Proposal Terms, Referral Partners, Marketing Results, Capacity Weeks and Pipeline by Month cover the rest of the sales year: days from enquiry to proposal, the reasons you lose, which source costs least per project, which partner sends paying work and whether the team has free hours for a new start date.

14 calculators cover fees, a fixed fee from hours, a percentage fee, an hourly estimate with a cap, proposal price, budget reality, payment schedule, win chance, counter-offers, scope changes, source cost, capacity, revision rounds and a fee what-if grid. Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and send 28 ready text messages that open with the details already written in.

This is part one of the Interior Designer suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data for a small design studio to explore first. It helps you plan your sales and does not promise results.

messages.moment: Client: thanks for your enquiry

messages.moment: Client: your design brief is ready

messages.moment: Client: your proposal is ready
messages.text: Hello {contact}, your proposal for the {project_type} project is ready. The design fee estimate is {fee_estimate} ({fee_type}). Shall we go through it together?

messages.moment: Client: your proposal is valid until

messages.moment: Client: the fee options explained

messages.moment: Client: your retainer secures the date
messages.text: Hello {client}, the retainer of {amount} secures your start date. It is due on {due_date} and is credited against your first fee invoice.

messages.moment: Client: your retainer has arrived
messages.text: Hello {client}, your retainer of {amount} arrived on {paid_on}. Welcome. We will confirm your start date and the kick-off meeting.

messages.moment: Client: we cannot start before this date
messages.text: Hello {contact}, we cannot start before {earliest_start} because our design team is full until then. Is that date fine for you?

messages.moment: Client: sorry we could not take it

messages.moment: Client: thank you for the referral

messages.moment: Client: your proposal change is attached

messages.moment: Client: a question about your budget
messages.text: Hello {contact}, a quick question about your budget: is {budget_est} for the whole {project_type} project, including delivery and installation?

messages.text: Hello, the proposal for {contact} expires on {valid_until}. Fee estimate {fee_estimate}. Chase check: {chase_flag}. Please decide whether to extend it.

documents.title: Design proposal and fee letter
paragraphs: Design proposal and fee letter of {set:company}, dated {today}.
Dear {col:proposals.contact}, thank you for the chance to design your {col:proposals.project_type} project. This letter sets out our proposal and our fee.

Fee model: {col:proposals.fee_type}. Design fee estimate: {col:proposals.fee_estimate}, which is {col:proposals.fee_share} of your estimated FF&E (furniture, fittings and equipment) budget of {col:proposals.ffe_budget_est}. The service lines add up to {col:proposals.lines_total}.
The earliest start date is {col:proposals.earliest_start}. A retainer secures the start date and is credited against the first fee invoice. Prices are before any tax.
This proposal is valid until {col:proposals.valid_until}. To accept it, sign below and return this letter with the retainer.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.

documents.title: Scope of services for a proposal
paragraphs: Scope of services of {set:company} for {col:proposals.contact}, dated {today}. Proposal {col:proposals.proposal_id}, {col:proposals.project_type}.
Stages: discovery and brief; concept design; design development; specification and approval; procurement; installation; styling and handover. Each stage ends with a written approval from you.
Fee model: {col:proposals.fee_type}. Fee estimate: {col:proposals.fee_estimate}. The fee includes the revision rounds shown in the terms; extra rounds are priced from our rate card.

Not included unless we agree it in writing: structural work, planning permission, items bought by you directly, and work outside the rooms in the brief. Anything extra is priced in a change order before it starts.
Your FF&E budget estimate is {col:proposals.ffe_budget_est}. Items are bought on our trade accounts and sold to you with a mark-up that we show on every purchase order.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.

documents.title: Fee comparison for a client
paragraphs: Fee comparison of {set:company} for the sample project {col:feemodels.name}, dated {today}. Type: {col:feemodels.project_type}, {col:feemodels.rooms} rooms, FF&E budget {col:feemodels.ffe_budget}, about {col:feemodels.est_hours} studio hours.
Fixed fee: {col:feemodels.fixed_fee}. You know the fee in advance and it changes only through a change order.
Hourly: about {col:feemodels.hourly_fee} on our estimate. You pay for the hours used, so a project that moves faster costs less and one that grows costs more. A cap can be agreed.
Percentage of the FF&E spend: about {col:feemodels.pct_fee}. The fee follows what is bought, so it grows and shrinks with your budget.
The lowest fee for you is the {col:feemodels.cheapest} model. We will help you choose the model that suits your project and your wish for certainty.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.

documents.title: Three package options for a budget
paragraphs: Three package options of {set:company} for {col:enquiries.contact}, dated {today}. Project: {col:enquiries.project_type}, about {col:enquiries.rooms_est} rooms. Your budget: {col:enquiries.budget_est}.
Essential: an FF&E budget of {col:enquiries.opt_ess}. Clean, durable choices with fewer custom pieces.
Refined: an FF&E budget of {col:enquiries.opt_ref}. More custom and trade-only pieces and a fuller lighting plan.
Luxury: an FF&E budget of {col:enquiries.opt_lux}. Bespoke joinery, premium fabrics and art, and the widest choice of vendors.
Your budget fits: {col:enquiries.fit}. Budget per room: {col:enquiries.budget_per_room}. We can phase the work if you prefer to start smaller.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.

documents.title: Consultation summary
paragraphs: Consultation summary of {set:company}, dated {today}.

Meeting on {col:consultations.date}: {col:consultations.kind}, {col:consultations.minutes} minutes, with {col:consultations.designer}. Contact: {col:consultations.contact}. Project type: {col:consultations.project_type}.

Notes of the meeting, the rooms visited and the points the client raised are written below.

Rooms: {col:briefs.rooms}. FF&E budget: {col:briefs.budget}, which is {col:briefs.budget_room} per room.
Deadline: {col:briefs.deadline}, {col:briefs.weeks_left} weeks from the brief. Deadline check: {col:briefs.deadline_flag}.
Decision makers: {col:briefs.decision_makers}. Must-haves: {col:briefs.must_haves}. Style in plain words: {col:briefs.style_notes}.
Please check every line. Your signature approves the brief as the basis of the concept design.

documents.title: Retainer invoice and terms

The retainer secures the start date of the project. It is credited against: {col:retainers.credited_against}. Fee type: {col:retainers.fee_type}.
After the concept stage starts the retainer is not refundable. Payment by bank transfer or card payment.
